newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Feb consumer credit rose $6.7 bln, or 6.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Feb consumer credit rose $6.7 bln, or 6.7 pct.

text.p: U.S. consumer installment credit rose in February by $6.7 billiion, or a 6.7 percent annual rate, from a revised $10.2 billion increase in January at a 10.3 percent rate, the Federal Reserve said on Monday.
The February increase matched the expectations of Wall Street economists surveyed by Reuters.
Previously, the Fed said January consumer credit had increased by $8.4 billion but it revised that up.

Revolving, or credit-card credit, rose by $5.1 billion at a 12.7 percent annual rate in February, the Fed said. Credit-card debt had surged by $8.4 billion at a 16-month high 21.6 percent rate in January.
Auto credit outstanding rose less than $100 million at a 0.3 percent annual rate February after rising in January by $1.0 billion at a 3.1 percent annual rate.

Other credit, which includes consumer bank loans like those for mobile homes and to pay for education but not real estate mortgages, rose by $1.6 billion at a 5.5 percent annual rate in February. In January, this category of credit rose by $800 million at a 2.9 percent annual rate.
Before seasonal adjustment, total outstanding consumer credit in February was $1.21 trillion, up from $1.12 trillion a year earlier in February 1996.
